title: Cluster work by contribution and risk

C1.rule: Mechanical, one owned file, fully specified, no design choice

C2.rule: Bounded implementation or tests, clear spec, one or two owned files and their tests

C3.rule: Cross-module design; changes a gate or the ledger contract; wrong means every project inherits it

C4.rule: Planning, merging, reconciling, anything in a project's real data, a sponsor decision

phases.name: Clusters
phases.goal: Work is scored by share and risk, the top 80% of share is built now, the tail runs in daily, weekly or when-touched batches, and checks run once per bundle.
phases.exit: C-01 to C-04 merged; one project's queue shows lanes and the cut line on its board.

phases.name: Research
phases.goal: Questions that need reading, not writing, before they become items, a proposal, or a decline.
phases.exit: Every X row is done only when it becomes items, a numbered proposal, or a recorded decline with the reason -- never a report nobody acted on.

items.title: Findings are catalogued, lane-sorted, triaged into batches and light-pathed
items.what: A finding -- from a review (quality-manager, any reviewer) or from testing (test-engineer bug reports, a failing or red-first test not yet fixed) -- is recorded as a row in the ledger, not only prose in a report or a chat message: an id, its source (`review`|`test`), file:line, severity, and `state` catalogued|decided|deferred|declined. Both kinds share one formula and one queue with items (C-01, C-02): share = value weight x points, risk = impact x likelihood (raised to 9 for anything restricted). `tracker lanes` sorts items, review findings and test findings together by share; the top 80% cumulative is Now, the rest fall to Daily/Weekly/When touched by risk, same cut line as C-02. A low-severity finding of either kind stays `catalogued` -- visible on the tracker page, not lost, not worked alone -- until the sponsor decides it (an ask, `state` decided). Once decided, if it is small (points 1-3, risk standard), it takes the light path (proposal 23 M-05) in a batch with other decided-small findings of either kind from the same cluster: one commit, one gate run, one log line, no separate reviewer, no per-item ceremony. A restricted or high-risk finding, from either source, is never light and never batched, same as C-02's alone rule. Before a batch of decided-small findings is worked, it is triaged, not just concatenated: findings that share a root cause, a file, or a pattern (the same missing check repeated, the same wrong default) are grouped and named as one cause with its own list of the findings it covers, so the batch fixes the cause once rather than patching each symptom separately. A finding that turns out to be a duplicate of, or subsumed by, another is marked `state: declined` with `duplicate_of` naming the survivor, not worked twice. Triage output is one line per group in the batch's log entry: the cause, the findings it covers, and the fix.
items.done: `tracker route`/`lanes` accept findings from both sources alongside items (a `kind: finding`, `source: review|test` row, or a light `findings` list on the ledger); a catalogued finding of either kind survives a `tracker lanes` run unworked until decided; decided-small findings from review and test both land in one batch on the light path; tests on a fixture mixing catalogued, decided-small (both sources) and decided-restricted findings, confirming they sort into one shared queue, not two. Triage: a fixture batch with three findings sharing one root cause groups to one line and one fix, not three; a duplicate finding is marked declined with duplicate_of and excluded from the count; the batch's log entry names each group's cause and coverage.

items.title: Two more statuses: in review, in testing
items.what: `tools/tracker/ledger.py`'s STATUSES gains two values between `in progress` and `done`: `in review` (with a reviewer, quality-manager or a review agent per C-05) and `in testing` (with test-engineer, or a red-first test not yet green). Purely additive -- every existing ledger using only the original four statuses stays valid and unaffected; nothing is renamed or removed. `counts()`/`status_line()` report both new buckets; `bin/tracker set --status` accepts them; `render.py`'s pill gets a colour for each, distinct from `blocked` (a stopped item) and `in progress` (a builder actively editing) -- these two mean the code is written and it is now elsewhere, waiting. C-05's catalogued/decided/deferred/declined states are for *findings*; this is for *items*, and the two are shown together on the board so a glance says who has what.
items.done: STATUSES, counts(), status_line(), render.py's pill and colour all updated; a ledger with only the four original statuses validates and renders exactly as before (regression test); tracker set --status in_review / --status in_testing works end to end on a fixture; the board shows both counts.
